topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, contextualises the lecture within the course, and outlines the core learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Conceptual Framework and Epidemiology of Cancer Causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational nature of cancer development, debating the relative contributions of random endogenous mutations versus environmental exposures supported by global epidemiological trends.

topics.label: Oncogenic Infectious Agents in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens promote malignancy, illustrating these mechanisms through the specific pathogenesis of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how various dietary, physical, and chemical agents interact with host metabolism to cause direct or oxidative DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic factors drive tumorigenesis by establishing permissive inflammatory environments, acting as tumor promoters, and exploiting specific host developmental states.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying Carcinogens and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to establish carcinogenicity and weigh environmental exposure risks.
